separable: separable — *color in the map*, and *color the map in*; with a pronoun it must split: *color it in*, never ✗ *color in it*.
gloss: To fill a drawn shape or outline with color.
examples: The kids *colored in* the whole map before lunch.
She *colors in* the shapes while I read to her.
He was *coloring* the dinosaur *in* with a green marker.

separable: inseparable — *comb through the files*, never ✗ *comb the files through*; a pronoun also stays after the particle: *comb through them*.
gloss: To search through something very carefully, looking at every part of it.
examples: Investigators *combed through* hours of security footage.
I'm *combing through* my inbox for the receipt.
She *combs through* the sales numbers every Monday morning.

ru: вызывать в памяти, вызвать; создавать как по волшебству
separable: separable — *conjure up an image*, and *conjure an image up*; with a pronoun it must split: *conjure it up*.
gloss: To bring a picture or memory into someone's mind, or to produce something as if by magic.
examples: The smell of cinnamon *conjures up* my grandmother's kitchen.
He *conjured up* a three-course dinner out of leftovers.
She has *conjured up* an excuse for every missed deadline.

separable: no object at all — intransitive, so nothing can stand between *conk* and *out*.
gloss: (Of a machine or engine) to stop working suddenly.
examples: The car *conked out* halfway up the hill.
My laptop *conks out* whenever the battery drops below ten percent.
The furnace has *conked out* twice this winter.

separable: no object at all — intransitive; the place follows: *conk out on the couch*.
gloss: To fall asleep suddenly because you are exhausted.
examples: He *conked out* on the couch before the movie ended.
The baby usually *conks out* in the car seat.
I was *conking out* at my desk by four o'clock.

ru: отдавать на подряд, отдать; передавать на сторону
separable: separable — *contract out the cleaning*, and *contract the cleaning out*; with a pronoun it must split: *contract it out*.
gloss: To pay an outside company to do work instead of doing it yourself.
examples: The city *contracts out* its snow removal.
They *contracted out* the whole help desk last spring.
We're *contracting out* payroll starting in June.

separable: separable — *cook up a story*, and *cook a story up*; with a pronoun it must split: *cook one up*.
gloss: To invent a story, excuse, or plan, usually a dishonest one.
examples: He *cooked up* a story about a flat tire.
They're *cooking up* some scheme to get out of the fee.
Whatever excuse she *cooks up*, don't believe a word of it.

separable: separable — *cook up some eggs*, and *cook some eggs up*; with a pronoun it must split: *cook them up*.
gloss: To prepare a meal quickly and without much fuss.
examples: I'll *cook up* some eggs if you're hungry.
She *cooked up* a huge pot of chili for the whole crew.
He's *cooking up* breakfast right now.

separable: separable when it takes an object — *cool down the engine*, *cool the engine down*, *cool it down*; when a person calms, there is no object at all: *let him cool down*.
transitivity: both — transitive (cool the engine down), intransitive (let him cool down)
gloss: To become calmer after being angry or excited, or to make something less hot.
examples: Give him an hour to *cool down* before you bring it up.
I *cooled* the soup *down* with a splash of cold water.
The engine has *cooled down* enough to touch.

separable: no object — intransitive in this sense; the angry person is the subject: *let her cool off*, never ✗ *cool her off* about the argument.
gloss: To become less angry after an argument.
examples: Let her *cool off* before you say anything else.
He went for a long walk to *cool off*.
By Monday they had *cooled off* and apologized.

ru: охладевать, охладеть; идти на спад, пойти на спад
separable: no object — intransitive; the thing losing steam is the subject: *the market cooled off*.
gloss: To become less active, less intense, or less enthusiastic.
examples: The housing market *cooled off* over the summer.
Her interest in the band is *cooling off* fast.
Sales *cool off* every year after the holidays.

separable: separable, and it usually splits — *coop the dog up*, *coop yourself up*; it lives mostly in the passive: *cooped up in a tiny apartment*.
gloss: To keep a person or animal shut inside a small space for too long.
examples: The kids have been *cooped up* all week by the rain.
Don't *coop* the dog *up* in the garage all day.
She *coops* herself *up* in the office and forgets to eat.

separable: no object — intransitive; what you are dodging follows *of*: *cop out of the interview*, never ✗ *cop the interview out*.
gloss: To avoid doing something you promised or should do, usually out of fear.
examples: He *copped out* at the last minute and sent an email instead.
Don't *cop out* now — you promised you'd speak.
She's *copping out* of the hard conversation again.

separable: separable — *copy down the address*, and *copy the address down*; with a pronoun it must split: *copy it down*.
gloss: To write down exactly what someone says or what is written somewhere else.
examples: *Copy down* the homework before the bell rings.
I *copied* the phone number *down* wrong.
He was *copying down* everything the professor said.

separable: separable — *cordon off the street*, and *cordon the street off*; with a pronoun it must split: *cordon it off*.
gloss: To close off an area with barriers or tape so that people cannot enter.
examples: Police *cordoned off* two blocks around the building.
They're *cordoning off* the street for the parade.
The whole wing gets *cordoned off* during the inspection.

separable: separable — *cough up the money*, and *cough the money up*; with a pronoun it must split: *cough it up*.
gloss: To hand over money or information that you did not want to give.
examples: We had to *cough up* two hundred dollars for the tow.
He finally *coughed up* the name of his supplier.
Nobody enjoys *coughing up* extra fees at checkout.

separable: mostly intransitive with *to* — *count down to New Year's*; with an object it can split (*count the days down*), though *count down the days* is far commoner.
transitivity: both — intransitive (count down to midnight), transitive (count down the days)
gloss: To count backward toward a moment you are waiting for.
examples: The crowd *counted down* from ten.
We're *counting down* the days until the trip.
She *counts down* to Friday every single week.

separable: separable, and it normally splits — *count me in*, *count Dave in*; ✗ *count in me* is impossible.
gloss: To include someone in a plan or activity.
examples: If you're ordering pizza, *count* me *in*.
They *counted* us *in* without even asking.
He's *counting* everyone *in* for Saturday's game.

separable: separable, and it normally splits — *count me out*, *count him out*; ✗ *count out me* is impossible.
gloss: To leave someone out of a plan or activity.
examples: If it starts before seven, *count* me *out*.
They *counted* him *out* of the weekend trip.
She's *counting* herself *out* of the potluck this time.

ru: сбрасывать со счетов, сбросить со счетов
separable: separable, and it normally splits — *don't count her out*; ✗ *count out her* is impossible.
gloss: To decide that someone has no chance of winning or succeeding.
examples: Don't *count* him *out* — he's come back from worse.
Everyone had *counted* the team *out* by halftime.
You'd be *counting* her *out* far too early.

separable: separable — *count up the votes*, and *count the votes up*; with a pronoun it must split: *count them up*.
gloss: To add together everything in a group to get a total.
examples: *Count up* the votes and tell me the total.
He *counted up* what he had spent and winced.
I'm *counting* the receipts *up* now.

separable: inseparable — *cover for me*, never ✗ *cover me for*; the person always follows *for*.
gloss: To do someone's job for them while they are away.
examples: Can you *cover for* me on Friday?
She *covered for* her boss all through August.
Who's *covering for* the front desk at lunch?

separable: inseparable — *cover for your brother*, never ✗ *cover your brother for*.
gloss: To lie or hide the truth in order to protect someone who has done something wrong.
examples: His partner *covered for* him for years.
Don't ask me to *cover for* you again.
She has been *covering for* her brother since high school.

separable: separable — *cover up the mistake*, and *cover the mistake up*; with a pronoun it must split: *cover it up*.
gloss: To hide a mistake, a crime, or an embarrassing fact so that others do not find out.
examples: The company tried to *cover up* the spill.
They *covered* it *up* for almost a decade.
He's terrible at *covering up* how he feels.

separable: separable when there is an object — *cover up your arms*, *cover them up*; just as often there is no object: *cover up, it's cold*.
transitivity: both — transitive (cover up your arms), intransitive (cover up, it's cold)
gloss: To put on more clothing, or to put cloth over part of the body.
examples: *Cover up* — it's thirty degrees out there.
She *covered* her shoulders *up* before going into the church.
He was *covering up* the sunburn with a long-sleeved shirt.

separable: inseparable — *cozy up to the boss*, never ✗ *cozy the boss up to*; the person always follows *to*.
gloss: To be very friendly to someone powerful in order to get something out of them.
examples: He's been *cozying up to* the new director all month.
The company *cozied up to* regulators for years.
She *cozies up to* whoever happens to be in charge.

ru: принимать жёсткие меры, принять; ужесточать борьбу (с)
separable: no object — intransitive; the target follows *on*: *crack down on speeding*, never ✗ *crack speeding down*.
gloss: To start dealing with bad behavior much more strictly.
examples: The city is *cracking down* on illegal parking.
Police *cracked down* hard after the second break-in.
Schools have *cracked down* on phones in class.

separable: separable — *crack open a beer*, and *crack a beer open*; with a pronoun it must split: *crack it open*.
gloss: To open a bottle, can, or container, especially a drink to enjoy.
examples: Let's *crack open* a bottle of wine.
He *cracked* a beer *open* and put his feet up.
They were *cracking open* sodas on the porch.

separable: no object — intransitive in this sense: *the whole room cracked up*.
gloss: To burst out laughing.
examples: The whole class *cracked up*.
I *crack up* every time I watch that scene.
She was *cracking up* before he even got to the punchline.

separable: separable, and it normally splits — *that joke cracks me up*; *it cracked up the whole table* is also fine, but a pronoun must sit in the middle: ✗ *crack up me*.
gloss: To make someone laugh a lot.
examples: That commercial *cracks* me *up*.
His impression of the boss *cracked* everyone *up*.
Stop — you're *cracking* me *up*.

ru: срываться, сорваться; не выдерживать, не выдержать (психически)
separable: no object — intransitive: *he cracked up under the pressure*.
gloss: To have a mental or emotional breakdown from stress.
examples: He nearly *cracked up* during finals week.
She's *cracking up* under the pressure of two jobs.
Two of them *cracked up* and quit before the season ended.

separable: inseparable — *cram for the test*, never ✗ *cram the test for*; the exam always follows *for*.
gloss: To study very hard for a short time right before a test.
examples: He *crammed for* the exam all night.
She's *cramming for* finals in the library.
I always *cram for* tests and regret it afterward.

separable: separable — *cram in three museums*, and *cram three museums in*; with a pronoun it must split: *cram them in*.
gloss: To fit more things or activities into a space or a period of time than it comfortably holds.
examples: We *crammed in* three museums before lunch.
He *crams* too much *in* on the first day of the trip.
They're *cramming* forty kids *in* one classroom.

ru: штамповать, наштамповать; выдавать в большом количестве
separable: separable — *crank out a report*, and *crank a report out*; with a pronoun it must split: *crank them out*.
gloss: To produce something quickly and in large amounts, usually without much care.
examples: The plant *cranks out* a thousand units a day.
He *cranked out* three articles before noon.
She's been *cranking out* sketches all week.

separable: separable — *crank up the heat*, and *crank the heat up*; with a pronoun it must split: *crank it up*.
gloss: To increase the volume, heat, or intensity of something.
examples: *Crank up* the heat — I'm freezing.
He *cranked* the music *up* until the windows rattled.
They're *cranking up* production for the holidays.

separable: separable — *crank up the generator*, and *crank the generator up*; with a pronoun it must split: *crank it up*.
gloss: To start a machine or an engine.
examples: He *cranked up* the generator when the power went out.
I'll *crank* the grill *up* in a few minutes.
She was *cranking up* the old tractor when we pulled in.

separable: no object — intransitive; the thing that appears is the subject: *a problem cropped up*.
gloss: To appear or happen unexpectedly.
examples: A problem *cropped up* with the permits.
Her name *crops up* in every other chapter.
Little delays keep *cropping up* as we get closer to launch.

separable: separable — *cross off the milk*, and *cross the milk off*; with a pronoun it must split: *cross it off the list*.
gloss: To remove an item or a name from a list because it is done or no longer needed.
examples: *Cross* the milk *off* the list — I already bought it.
She *crossed off* three names before noon.
He's *crossing* chores *off* as he finishes them.

separable: separable — *cross out the wrong answer*, and *cross the wrong answer out*; with a pronoun it must split: *cross it out*.
gloss: To draw a line through something written because it is wrong or no longer wanted.
examples: *Cross out* the wrong answer and write the right one above it.
He *crossed* my name *out* with a red pen.
She had *crossed out* half the paragraph.

ru: переходить, перейти (на другую сторону, в другой жанр)
separable: no object — intransitive; where you move to follows *to* or *into*: *cross over to jazz*.
gloss: To move from one side, group, or style to another.
examples: She *crossed over* from country music to pop.
Every year a few senators *cross over* to vote with the other party.
The show has *crossed over* to a much younger audience.

separable: separable — *crowd out the small shops*, and *crowd the small shops out*; with a pronoun it must split: *crowd them out*.
gloss: To take up so much room or attention that something else is left with none.
examples: The big chains *crowded out* the local bookstores.
Test prep is *crowding* art *out* of the school day.
Cheap imports have *crowded out* domestic makers.

separable: no object — intransitive; the reason follows *in* or *with*: *cry out in pain*.
gloss: To make a loud sound suddenly because of pain, fear, or surprise.
examples: He *cried out* when the nurse touched his shoulder.
She *cries out* in her sleep sometimes.
Someone was *crying out* two floors below.

separable: inseparable — *crying out for repairs*, never ✗ *cry repairs out for*; what is needed always follows *for*.
gloss: To need something so badly that the need is obvious to everyone.
examples: This kitchen is *crying out for* a coat of paint.
The system *cried out for* reform long before anyone acted.
Small towns like ours *cry out for* doctors.

separable: no object — intransitive; the person or animal follows *to*, *with*, or *next to*: *cuddle up to the dog*.
gloss: To lie or sit very close to someone for warmth or affection.
examples: The kids *cuddled up* under one blanket.
She *cuddles up* to the dog every night.
They were *cuddling up* on the couch watching a movie.

ru: ставить на воспроизведение, поставить; готовить к запуску
separable: separable — *cue up the next song*, and *cue the next song up*; with a pronoun it must split: *cue it up*.
gloss: To get a song, video, or clip ready so that it starts at the right moment.
examples: *Cue up* the next song.
He had already *cued up* the video before the meeting started.
She's *cuing up* the slides for the talk.

separable: no object — intransitive; what you settle with follows *with*: *curl up with a book*.
gloss: To settle into a comfortable position with your arms and legs pulled in close.
examples: She *curled up* with a book and a blanket.
The cat *curls up* on the warm laptop every afternoon.
He has *curled up* in that same chair every evening this week.
